title: COPD, respiratory failure and home oxygen
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's chronic lung disease and any respiratory failure or oxygen dependence.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic respiratory conditions.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and associated respiratory issues. He reports that his breathing remains consistent with his baseline. He continues to use home oxygen for management of his chronic respiratory failure. He reports that he is able to perform activities of daily living with reasonable ease, though he experiences shortness of breath during exertion. He denies any recent changes in his cough, sputum production, or significant changes in his oxygen requirements. He reports adherence to his current medication regimen.

Medication List
1. Tiotropium and Fluticasone inhaler
2. Albuterol HFA as needed
3. Home oxygen (continuous)

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or unintended weight loss.
Respiratory: Positive for chronic shortness of breath; negative for productive cough or chest pain.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations or edema.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness or confusion.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his spouse. He is a former smoker who quit several years ago. He enjoys watching television and light gardening.

Family History
Father had hypertension and coronary artery disease. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.2 F
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 78 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 18 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 92% on home oxygen
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 13.8 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
eGFR: 62 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: The patient is alert and oriented x3, appearing in no acute distress.
Respiratory: Lung sounds are diminished in the lower lobes with scattered wheezes noted. No accessory muscle use.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; S1 and S2 are distinct.
Extremities: No cyanosis or peripheral edema noted.

Assessment
1. COPD: Stable. The patient’s chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is well-managed at this time.
2. Chronic respiratory failure: The patient continues to demonstrate chronic respiratory failure. He remains hypoxic on room air and requires continuous home oxygen to maintain adequate systemic oxygenation.

Plan
1. Continue current maintenance medications.
2. Continue use of home oxygen as prescribed.
3. Follow up in three months for a repeat evaluation of respiratory status.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia: J96.11 (HCC 213), plus Z99.81 for the home oxygen.
